title: The nine-value ladder
goal: Separate nine values with controlled layers, including untouched paper.

steps.title: Read the extremes
steps.text: Value 1 is untouched paper; 9 is your deepest usable graphite. Screen tones are only a guide: glare, brightness and pencil brand change how values appear.
steps.talk: Read the extremes. Value 1 is untouched paper; 9 is your deepest usable graphite. Screen tones are only a guide: glare, brightness and pencil brand change how values appear. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Can you identify the lightest and darkest samples?
steps.check: Can you identify the lightest and darkest samples?

steps.title: Draw nine boxes
steps.text: Lightly mark nine equal boxes about 2 cm wide. Leave gaps between them so neighbouring tones do not contaminate your judgement.
steps.talk: Draw nine boxes. Lightly mark nine equal boxes about 2 cm wide. Leave gaps between them so neighbouring tones do not contaminate your judgement. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the construction lines light enough to disappear?
steps.check: Are the construction lines light enough to disappear?

steps.title: Anchor light, middle, dark
steps.text: Keep box 1 blank. Build box 5 with HB and 2B. Build box 9 with repeated 4B and 6B layers, without polishing the surface.
steps.talk: Anchor light, middle, dark. Keep box 1 blank. Build box 5 with HB and 2B. Build box 9 with repeated 4B and 6B layers, without polishing the surface. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Do the three anchors remain distinct when you squint?
steps.check: Do the three anchors remain distinct when you squint?

steps.title: Insert five values
steps.text: Add boxes 3 and 7, placing each visually halfway between its neighbours. Judge the relationships rather than counting pencil passes.
steps.talk: Insert five values. Add boxes 3 and 7, placing each visually halfway between its neighbours. Judge the relationships rather than counting pencil passes. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 ordered from light to dark?
steps.check: Are 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 ordered from light to dark?

steps.title: Complete nine values
steps.text: Fill boxes 2, 4, 6 and 8. Alternate the stroke direction gently to reduce gaps. Use softer graphite for deeper tones, not extra force.
steps.talk: Complete nine values. Fill boxes 2, 4, 6 and 8. Alternate the stroke direction gently to reduce gaps. Use softer graphite for deeper tones, not extra force. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Is every adjacent pair visibly different?
steps.check: Is every adjacent pair visibly different?

steps.title: Even the layers
steps.text: Fill pale gaps with small overlapping strokes. A clean stump may lightly soften a patch, but do not blend across the gaps between boxes.
steps.talk: Even the layers. Fill pale gaps with small overlapping strokes. A clean stump may lightly soften a patch, but do not blend across the gaps between boxes. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the centres and corners of each box similar in value?
steps.check: Are the centres and corners of each box similar in value?

steps.title: Lift a correction
steps.text: If a box is too dark, dab it gently and rebuild. Protect box 1 from graphite on your fingers.
steps.talk: Lift a correction. If a box is too dark, dab it gently and rebuild. Protect box 1 from graphite on your fingers. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does box 1 still match clean paper?
steps.check: Does box 1 still match clean paper?

steps.title: Check under one light
steps.text: Tilt the sheet slightly to detect graphite shine. Return it flat and compare with a small viewing hole cut in scrap paper to isolate each box.
steps.talk: Check under one light. Tilt the sheet slightly to detect graphite shine. Return it flat and compare with a small viewing hole cut in scrap paper to isolate each box. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are you judging tone rather than reflected glare?
steps.check: Are you judging tone rather than reflected glare?

steps.title: Use the scale
steps.text: Choose a mug and match its light, middle and shadow to three boxes. Make a tiny three-value thumbnail before attempting detail.
steps.talk: Use the scale. Choose a mug and match its light, middle and shadow to three boxes. Make a tiny three-value thumbnail before attempting detail. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Can you state which three values describe the mug?
steps.check: Can you state which three values describe the mug?

source: Original procedural instructional study; no external reference photograph.
drill: Repeat the study at half size without the grid. Compare your darkest dark, lightest light and largest shape before adding detail.
